exposure: mode of delivery in first birth (elective cesarean vs. other)
mode of delivery in second birth (elective repeat cesarean, vaginal birth, unplanned repeat cesarean)
outcome: birth experience (measured by visual analogue scale (VAS) score)
negative birth experience (defined as VAS score ≤5)
cohort: 808 women with a first cesarean and eligible for trial of labor after cesarean (TOLAC) in Sweden from 2014-2017
finding: While most women reported a positive birth experience regardless of delivery mode, women who had an unplanned repeat cesarean delivery had a five-fold higher odds of a negative birth experience compared to those with an elective repeat cesarean.
mod_finding: Women having an unplanned repeat cesarean delivery had five-fold higher odds of negative birth experience compared to women having an elective repeat cesarean.
